status.en: 28 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 75% more than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Merti.

summary.en: Violence in northern Ethiopia continues to push the health system toward collapse as WHO warns it is near failure, while renewed drone strikes from Ethiopia target Sudan and an Amhara displacement camp and civilians gathering grain in Tigray. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has sent senior ministers to military training in Hurso and Ethiopia is accused of using Assosa Airport as a launch base for RSF drones and supplying arms to the RSF. An RPG fired near a school in Moyale killed 60 Ethiopian Orthodox believers, prompting the Orthodox Church to demand action. The conflict has displaced 1.7 million Ethiopians and affected an additional 173,000 people, according to UNHCR, and there were 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
